answer: A haven is worth only the hulls that actually docked there. Each newcomer must arrive with a manifest countersigned by two distinct vessels already moored, and the harbour compares manifests, so aliases carrying one vessel's papers merge into a single berth and one vote. The k-th berth an operator claims costs k squared in bond, so n heads need n distinct countersigners and near n cubed in escrow. A horizon sample hides which quay is inspected each epoch, and every berth must keep a mirror of its cargo log public; a mirror that omits a landing voids the whole haven.
